rationale: The CORS configuration of a function URL lists the web origins whose pages a browser will let read the response. Setting it to "*" hands that permission to every site on the internet, so a page under someone else's control can call the endpoint from a visitor's browser and read what comes back. On a URL that requires IAM authentication the caller still needs credentials, but any page holding them - a single-page application, an extension - can now be the one making the call; on a URL open to anyone, the allowlist was the only thing keeping third-party pages from using the endpoint as their own backend, whether to reach data it returns or to spend the concurrency of the account.
remediation: List the origins that legitimately call the function in the CORS AllowOrigins of the URL configuration instead of "*", and keep AllowCredentials off unless the browser genuinely has to send cookies
